slides.texte_overlay:
How to become ridiculously
social in your 20s
Say yes to the second invitation. The first one you might skip, but the second one you go to, no excuses. Most friendships start because someone simply kept showing up.
Join something that meets every week. A run club, a five-a-side team, a language class. Seeing the same faces weekly turns strangers into friends without any awkward effort.
Talk to the people next to you. In a queue, at a bar, in the gym. "Is this line always this slow?" Ninety percent of the time people are happy to chat. You just have to start.
Be the one who organises. Book the table, start the group chat, pick the date. Social guys aren't always the most popular. They're the ones who make things actually happen.
Remember names and use them. "Good to see you again, Luca." Repeat the name in your head when you hear it. People feel seen, and they start looking forward to seeing you too.
Always have something new to talk about. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you'll never run out of conversation, at a party, a dinner or a first meeting.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: standing in the corner with nothing to say. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I never run out of conversation.

slides.texte_overlay: Follow up after you meet someone. "Great talking yesterday, let's get that coffee." Most people mean to and never do. A single message turns a nice chat into an actual friend.
